findings.issue: The two authorities disagree on the 409 body. Line 37 of the CTG5 contract fixes the 409 mismatch body as { code: configuredMismatchCode, context: { key } }, and the implementation matches it: reject(409, { code, context }) at packages/backend/src/transactional-command/transactional-command.ts:404, and IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_PROGRESS at :355/:395/:407. law/schemas/error-envelope.schema.json requires { statusCode, errorCode, message, requestId } with additionalProperties:false on every 4xx/5xx. Its errorCode pattern is <DOMAIN>:<CATEGORY>:<detail>, and the default 'IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT' does not match it. Under the authority order (constitution > ADR > law/schemas > development-contract > docs/framework/contracts), the schema outranks the CTG5 contract. Within 1.5.0 the new surfaces also disagree: CTG6 docs/framework/contracts/web-kit-1.5.md:9 treats the schema as authoritative and requires its new 428/412 responses to use the law shape, while CTG5 adds new non-conforming 409s. Two things lower the severity but do not settle the question. First, the existing global StynxErrorFilter in packages/core/src/error.filter.ts already emits { code, message, context } and passes HttpException bodies through, so the schema was already not enforced. Second, UPS-TXN-03 only requires a 409 with a configurable code. The new interop test correctly asserts the CTG5 reviewed contract, so this is a CTG5/law reconciliation gap, not a CTG7 defect. CTG7 does not create or own this shape.
findings.required_change: Do not block ordered cumulative import of CTG7. Before the final full CI and 1.5.0 publication, the Owner must record a decision (INV-ERROR-001 change_policy requires human_approval and forbids test weakening). Recommended option A: the Architect amends the CTG5 contract so mismatch and in-progress 409s emit the law envelope, e.g. { statusCode:409, errorCode:'IDEMPOTENCY:CONFLICT:key-mismatch' | 'IDEMPOTENCY:CONFLICT:in-progress', message, requestId, details:{ key }, retryable:false }. mismatchCode stays configurable but is validated against the schema pattern at boot, and errors.json and the migration notes are updated. An Inspector then updates the CTG5 sensors and packages/backend/test/integration/angular-transactional-command-http.spec.ts to assert the complete new envelope exactly, which strengthens the assertion rather than removing it. An Engineer changes reject(), and the Architect rebinds trace and API baselines. Option B: an Owner-approved ADR records a scoped exception for transactional-command rejections and the legacy StynxErrorFilter shape, and a DEVAI Architect law/ commit amends the schema description ('Every stynx HTTP endpoint') to name that exception. Under either option, add the decision to the C-0002 §7 conformance ledger. Changing the law schema or the 409 test without one of these decisions is not acceptable.

summary: HEAD 21f518aa descends from the CTG6 PASS receipt e500c894. The 56-file delta is limited to CTG7 scope plus the new interop sensor. All five MUST items under OD-S15-01 are proven. UPS-HOOK-01: packages/integration-adapter/src/webhook-signature.ts HMACs the raw bytes (default is '<10-digit ts>.' followed by rawBody, with no reparse), enforces /^sha256=[0-9a-f]{64}$/i, and compares with timingSafeEqual only after the grammar check. It applies an inclusive |now-ts|<=maxSkewMs window with an injected clock, and an invalid clock throws. It makes one atomic consume, keyed by namespace:ts:recomputed-hex with the specified expiresAt. It returns six stable reason codes, and a store outage becomes WebhookReplayStoreError with no secret material in the message. UPS-HOOK-02: the guard clears every identity field and the public-tenant marker before verifying. It maps rejections to 401, store failure to 503, and clock or callback errors to 500, and validates options at bootstrap. The Nest integration test covers two applications sharing one replay store and a migrated PostgreSQL FORCE RLS table queried as stynx_app, where two signed tenants each see only their own row. It also shows real auth.memberships 403 TENANT_ACCESS_DENIED for a nonmember and for header/claim divergence. UPS-CAL-01: @stynx-nyx/core exports Clock, SystemClock, STYNX_CLOCK and provideStynxClock. UPS-CAL-02: TenantBusinessCalendar takes host-supplied timezone and holidays, with no STYNX holiday catalog and no Date.now. It steps by civil day and finds the first valid instant by binary search, which handles skipped and repeated midnight; there are Cairo and New York vectors. It rejects offset zones by the raw-string check and after Intl resolution, which closes the U+2212 bypass with a sensor, and fails closed on source errors. UPS-NGIDEM-01: the interceptor is opt-in through the HttpContext token only, for POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE, skipping SSE and never overwriting an existing header. The body-hash variant is explicit (includeBodyHash:true, JSON object or array, application/json). canonicalJson sorts keys by code point, maps -0 to 0, applies toJSON, and rejects non-JSON values. provideStynxIdempotency rejects duplicate registration. The new interop sensor uses the real IdempotencyKeyInterceptor to produce the key. It sends live HTTP to Nest @TransactionalCommand, with the app pool connected as stynx_app against migrated PostgreSQL. It proves the handler ran once, with one audit.events row and one tenant-scoped core.idempotency_keys row. The replay is byte-identical with idempotency-replayed:true, and reusing the key with a changed body returns an actual 409 with the CTG5 envelope. The test fails hard without PostgreSQL. Production code has no source-deep imports and there is no DETRAN code. The changeset covers all five fixed-group packages, and READMEs, baselines, trace and focused RLS gates are evidenced. Per the brief, test:int 51/51, rls-negative (7 tables), rls-smoke and the focused 1/1 have logs at this HEAD; baselines 44/44 and trace 448/448 are reported as passed. The 409 envelope conflict between the CTG5 contract and law/schemas/error-envelope.schema.json is real, because law/schemas outranks docs/framework/contracts. CTG7 neither introduces nor owns that conflict, so it does not block ordered CTG7 import. It does block final 1.5.0 publication until the Owner decides between law-conforming 409s (recommended, and consistent with CTG6's 428/412) and an ADR-scoped exception, without weakening the 409 test. The remaining findings are nonblocking hardening and evidence-attribution items. Verdict: CTG7 HEAD is safe for ordered cumulative import under OD-S15-02; full CI, the PR, remote CI and publication stay deferred.
